key_insight: A small, reproducible RNA splicing signature can distinguish ReNU syndrome cases from controls and act as a quantitative biomarker, especially for variants in the U4-2 T-loop.
clinical_relevance: This biomarker could support therapeutic development and future trial readouts by providing a measurable RNA-based indicator of disease-specific splicing defects.
method: Analyzed RNA-seq from two independent ReNU cohorts plus control samples.
Identified shared alternative splicing events, focusing on alternative 5' splice-site (A5SS) changes.
Derived a minimal six-site signature and tested it in patient-derived iPSC-to-neuron models.
evidence_signal: Across 30 individuals with ReNU syndrome and 54 controls, the six-site signature perfectly separated 19 n.64_65insT cases from controls and showed no false positives in 5,984 additional whole-blood controls.
watch_item: The signature appears specific to certain RNU4-2 T-loop variants, so broader validity across all ReNU genotypes and clinical settings still needs confirmation.
paper_title: A cross-tissue splicing signature as a quantitative biomarker for ReNU syndrome
